recipes.name: Charley's Slow Cooker Mexican Style Meat

steps.text: Trim the roast of any excess fat, and season with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Place the beef in the hot skillet, and brown it quickly on all sides.

Transfer the roast to a slow cooker and top it with the chopped onion. Season with chile peppers, chili powder, cayenne pepper, hot pepper sauce, and garlic powder. Add enough water to cover 1/3 of the roast.

Cover, and cook on High for 6 hours, checking to make sure there is always at least a small amount of liquid in the bottom of the cooker. Reduce heat to Low, and continue cooking for 2 to 4 hours, or until meat is totally tender and falls apart.
Transfer the roast to a bowl and shred it using two forks (reserve 2 cups of cooking liquid, if desired).
Serve in tacos or burritos (see Cook's Note).

raw_recipe.headline: Charley's Slow Cooker Mexican Style Meat
raw_recipe.description: A hot and spicy chuck roast that can be made into burritos, tacos, or any number of other Mexican-style dishes.

review.reviewBody:
Incredible. I'm from San Diego, so must, must, MUST have lots of flavor and spice in my meat, 'cause I'm used to it! Can't throw a rock without running into authentic Mexican food here. The flavor of this is just like that juicy, spiced shredded beef you dream of. Not-blow-your-head-off hot to my palette. Just right.

Cooking time: using a 3 pounder, we cooked 8 hours on low overnight. At 8 hours, the meat was falling apart; removed it, shredded with two forks, spooned off the fat in the Crock pot, removed a majority of the onions/peppers via a slotted spoon, returned mixture to Crock Pot juice and cooked on low for 1 1/2 hours. This is important; it allows the spiced juice that has formed overnight to really get in that meat.

Spices: used a 5 oz. bottle of Tapatio hot sauce. Increased chili powder to 1 TBS and added 1 1/2 tsp. of cumin, because what's Mex without cumin? Green peppers: used de-seeded chopped fresh jalapenos. Added a beef boullion cube like other posters recommended.

When you replace the beef, now shredded, into the pot to simmer, add 1/2 tsp. of additional cumin and 1 tsp. of paprika. Trust me, this is key.

Best part: your first meal of the morning can be Machaca; combine a handful of shredded beef, 4 eggs (beaten), 1/2 cup of veggies of your choice (we used onion/yellow pepper), stir in pan till done, spoon into ripped up flour tortillas and eat.

I have been using this recipe for 2 years now. It is excellent when chicken is substituted & paired with the Red Enchilada Sauce (also on this site) for a outstanding chicken enchilada dish. 

Also, whenever chuck roast goes on sale, I buy one & cook it with this recipe & then use it for the beef filling in the Beef Tamales on this site as well. It makes a lot, so I freeze half of them in gallon size freezer bags - then when I want to eat one, I just steam it for about 15 minutes - so good! They hold in the freezer for 6 months. 

This really is a wonderful base recipe that you can use with all meats to make fillings for all sorts of dishes. And, its easy!

I used my electric pressure cooker to make this and it turned out amazing! I browned the sides using the "sauté" setting, then I switched the setting to "meat/stew" to finished the slow cooker process. I was feeding several children that night, so I didn't put in as much of the Mexican hot sauce. I also didn't have any diced green chilis around the house, so I used a large can of green enchilada sauce instead. I thought the flavor and texture was amazing! I got amazing reviews from my sister and her family as well as all of mine. I will definitely recommend this!

This is super yummy! I bought a 5lb chuck roast from Costco and cut it into 4 pieces, then seasoned and seared before adding to the crock pot- which I lined with a crock pot liner for easier clean up.. I only quartered the onions, so I could remove them later on, I also used minced garlic instead of garlic powder and I used beef broth instead of water. I cooked it on low for about 8-10 hours (overnight). Once the meat was tender enough to shred, I removed the pieces of meat and put onto a large plate and I also removed the bag of cooking liquid and put it aside. I put a new crockpot liner inside the pot and I shredded the meat (removing the fat) and added it back to the crockpot, then ladled several spoonful's of the cooking liquid back to the meat (straining it while doing so), to keep the meat moist and remove the large pieces of onions. I used it to make street tacos and it was delicious. Not too spicy at all! Next time, I think I'll try the suggestion another reviewed game, adding some cumin and paprika to the meat after shredding it, to give it some more flavor.

Perfect as is. I only had a 2 pound roast so I cooked it in my deep cast iron pan for 2 hours, covered. Shredded the meat, added the additional cumin & cooked for another half hour or so, uncovered. I did adjust the seasonings for taste & small roast. There are only 2 of us & we've used it for tacos, taquitos, burritos. I tried a quick fry, like in stir fry. Fantastic. Next time I will use a 4 pound & use the crock pot for more leftovers. Note: I took out the onions & smashed them with a fork. The very tough ones I tossed, the tender mush went right back into the meat. Yum.

Oh Charley, this recipe is a WINNER! I used a grass fed chuck roast and followed your recipe closely, except I was intrigued by another reviewer who added beer instead of water, so I did that (a half can of Guinness stout). I also added a few packets of concentrated beef stock, lots more cumin, and some adobe spice. Went just shy of the total amount of hot sauce, and all we had was Red Hot. I was worried it would taste like buffalo sauce, but it didn't. It was just a wonderful medley of flavors! I also didn't have any fresh peppers, so I added two small cans of the mild diced chiles. Flipped it half way through the high heat phase, took the meat out after 6 hours on high, shredded it, stirred in a slurry of corn starch to thicken the sauce a bit, and threw the shredded meat back in on low for the 2 hours as directed. Hubbs and I both LOVED the meat. This will be on regular rotation in our household. Given the fact that your recipe can turn a cheap piece of meat into gold, I'd give this recipe ten stars if I could!

I changed mine a lot. I seasoned with smoked sea salt and creole seasoning then browned it. Then I re-seasoned the meat with the salt, pepper, creole, lots of fresh ground cumin, some rosemary, and extra smoked paprika. I deglazed the pan with beef stock. 

I trussed the trimmed meat tightly using cooking twine, placed in a 14" covered deep skillet. I covered the meat with the fresh chopped onions, a shallot, some garlic salt and 2/3'rds special beef stock that was pre-cooked with some cumin, onions, shallots, shredded carrots, and other various stew spices. 

Cooked in a 250F convection oven for 55 minutes (temp tested beef rare). Cut in half and cooled for an hour. Then placed in 2 food storage containers with the stock (1/2 in each) and refrigerated overnight. Mine did not shred like a slow cooker, but it sliced easily. Heated in the juice and served in flour tacos w/ lettuce, cilantro, avocado, sour cream, lime juice, and lime salsa.

The key to this recipe is to spice to your taste. I don't like hot, but I loaded up on the creole because the meat needs to flavor through. That is why I seasoned and browned it after cutting out the fat and then seasoned it again before trussing. That is also why you only cook it rare and let it sit overnight. It needs to absorb the flavor. That way you don't overcook it during the reheat in the microwave.

I’ve tried this with beef and pork. It has a great taste, shreds easy and lasts for a few days in the fridge. I looked at several other recipes, liked this one, and then modified it for taste and time. Unless you like really spicy, forget the habanero sauce. It’s probably more spice than most norteños would like. Instead I used half a can of Hatch diced jalapeños and a whole can of Hatch mild green chilies. Adjust the jalapeños to suit your taste. I also skipped the sear of the roast. Instead, just cover the bottom of the slow cooker with olive oil, place the roast in the middle, sprinkle the mixed herbs over the roast, and then cover it with the the chilies. Let it cook for 4 to 6 hours on low. Add a little water (1/2 cup or so) after a couple of hours to keep it from drying out. This is perfect for tacos (the traditional tortillas from Sprouts are the best!). Add a little sour cream to cut the heat, a little lettuce or cabbage, and your favorite salsa. You’ll swear they just came off your favorite street taco truck.

This recipe is off the chart good! I did make a few changes. I browned my chuck roast in a cast iron skillet. After removing the roast I tossed in 1 Tbsp butter and sautéed a very thinly sliced onion for approximately 3 minutes until translucent and fairly caramelized before removing from the pan. I then deglazed the pan with 1 1/2 cups water allowing it to simmer 3 to 5 to slightly reduce before adding it to the slow cooker. I did include 1 1/2 tsp cumin, substituted the green chili with a entire 28 ounce can of mild green enchilada sauce, tossed in 2 tsp. beef bouillon, and decreased the red hot sauce to 3 ounces. I'm tough, but I'm not that tough. I can't get enough of this stuff. Thank you! Thank you! Thank you!

Used 2oz Texas pete instead of 5 and adjusted other hot spices accordingly. Served as taco meat with Lettuce, Tomato, onion sour cream and grated cheddar. Messy but good. If i knew how to fold burritos it would have been perfect.

After 4 tries I have been able to create both the young and restless (close to exact recipe) and the Old Geezer version reducing the quantity of spices and forgetting the cayenne. Now trying vacuum seal smaller portions and freeze them and grab them for a night we are busy using the sous vide method. We'll see if it works.

I really, really wanted tacos for Cinco De Mayo but I didn't have all the ingredients for this recipe :( I decided to improvise and I'm sure glad I did because it was AMAZING. I used a 2.5lb London Broil (didn't sear on the stove just trimmed some fat & threw it in the bottom of the slow cooker) and covered it with a packet of taco seasoning, a generous dash of cumin, 2-3 cloves minced garlic and enough water to submerge about 1/3 of the roast. I then cooked it on low for 12 hours, took it out to shred the meat & skim some fat off the water, then put the shrewd meat back in the water on low for another 2hours. The meat we got was so moist and flavorful that's family is now obsessed & wants me to cook it every time we have "taco night"! If you have the chance to cook for a long time, please do, it's soooo worth it!
Love it. It has earned a spot in the dinner rotation.

I've been making this recipe since 2008 & still use this recipe as my main squeeze for nachos, tacos, burritos & tamales. Sometimes I'll use pork shoulder instead of beef & it's just as wonderful. If I forget to thaw meat I throw it in frozen, skipping the searing. I've made it in a pressure cooker too. From frozen, on high pressure for 60 minutes because my cooker is old & things still seem a little tough if I do 40 minutes.
Loved the spice with this meat! We used it for tacos and everyone loved it.

Came out killer. Only thing i did different was also add chipotle in adobo in it and used beeth broth instead of water and tapatio as the pepper sauce. Stuff came out great, moving from cali to north carolina hard to find decent mexican food here impossible. THis isn't it but this hit that itch for sure. Wasn't spicy at all to me i don't know all the complaints lol. I'm going throug this saying no flavor. I guess because i don't ever follow recipes to a T, i alter to what i think could be added. Like beef stock instead of water. Chiplote in adobe, i used tapatio, though next time i'l make my own hot sauce with habaneros. I also used this for burritos so i did use the sauce with the meat on a skillet after and cooked it down to a glaze sauce.
I followed Impish's suggestions and it was great!

I used Tapatio as the hot pepper sauce & used a 7 oz can of the green chiles instead of fresh. This was soooo good but def Spicy! Great for me not so much for my kids lol next time I will use a more mild hot sauce for them and maybe less than 5oz or just up the water. I ended up using the leftovers to make an easy birria ramen which in my opinion was even BETTER than the burritos! Definitely will make it again!

This has become a family favorite. I've made it many times. You can use different kinds of peppers and pepper sauce. I like to use a little beef broth instead of just water. If there is too much liquid I remove most of it before shredding the beef. It always comes out very tender and delicious.
I have been making this for years, love the recipe! Was wondering if any one has tried converting to an Instant Pot?
